rows.question: What's the difference between talking to you and Coder?
how do I connect my Mac
Can I link my linux box so the agent can work on it?
I ran coder host serve --tailnet-admission standard but my Mac never shows up on the phone. What should I check?
rows.reply:
Here is what you should check:

- **Tailscale connection:** Make sure your phone is connected to Tailscale through the Tailscale app, and that both your phone and Mac are on the same tailnet [openagents.connect-computer, openagents.tailnet].
- **Tailnet sign-in:** Confirm that you have signed in on the Tailnet screen under Account in the OpenAgents app [openagents.connect-computer].
- **Same Tailscale user:** Tailnet admission only works if both devices belong to the same Tailscale user, because the host will only answer a device that `tailscale whois` identifies as its own user [openagents.connect-computer, openagents.tailnet].

If it still does not appear, you can add it manually in **Account > Computers > Add a computer** using an invitation or an 8-character code [openagents.connect-computer].

rows.question: how do I install coder on my laptop
rows.reply:
To install Coder on your computer, run `./scripts/install-coder.sh` from a checkout of our open-source repository [openagents.install-coder]. This builds `crates/coder` in release mode with the pinned toolchain and links `~/.openagents/bin/coder` to the new build [openagents.install-coder]. 

Make sure `~/.openagents/bin` is on your `PATH` [openagents.install-coder]. 

After installation, run `coder host serve --tailnet-admission standard` so your phone can reach the computer over your tailnet [openagents.install-coder]. You can verify the installation with `coder --version` or `coder doctor` [openagents.install-coder].

which model does coder use on my computer
rows.reply:
Coder uses the engine and model configured by your computer's owner on the host [openagents.coder-engines]. 

The host sends each task to a connected model provider with capacity, failing over to another when one runs out [openagents.coder-engines]. The model cannot be chosen from your phone, and there is no model picker in the app yet [openagents.coder-engines].

rows.question: Can I pick GPT or Claude for Coder from my phone?
I sent a task to my computer and nothing happened, it just sits there
rows.reply:
A task sent from your phone runs right away only if the computer's owner has turned on the host's auto-start policy using a command on the computer [openagents.auto-start]. 

Without that policy enabled, the task is simply recorded and will not run by itself [openagents.auto-start]. Once auto-start is turned on, Coder runs at once in the workspaces listed by the policy [openagents.auto-start].

why did that last answer show up so fast
rows.reply:
Responses usually appear quickly for a few main reasons:

1. **Streaming:** The text is sent to your screen word-by-word (token-by-token) as it is generated, rather than waiting for the entire message to be finished.
2. **Specialized Hardware:** AI models run on powerful hardware (like GPUs or TPUs) optimized specifically for high-speed text processing and generation.
3. **Prompt Complexity:** Shorter, more straightforward prompts require less computation and generate fewer tokens, making the turnaround time noticeably faster.

rows.question: Is the wallet custodial?
What happens to my funds if Breez goes out of business?
what is spark
rows.reply:
Spark is the system our Wallet runs on instead of running a Lightning node of your own, while your keys stay on your phone [openagents.wallet-trust]. 

Its operators are run by three companies—Lightspark, Breez, and Flashnet—and two must cooperate for off-chain payments [openagents.wallet-trust]. If the operators ever stop, you can still withdraw your funds on-chain yourself [openagents.wallet-trust].

What level am I and how do levels work?
rows.reply:
You can check your current level by going to **Account > Trainer**, which displays your trainer card with your level, XP, and progress to the next level [openagents.trainer-card]. 

Here is how levels work:
- Everyone starts at level 1 [openagents.trainer-card].
- Level 2 is unlocked at 100 XP, level 3 at 283 XP, and level 4 at 520 XP [openagents.trainer-card].
- Levels follow `trainer-curve-v1`, and anyone can recompute them from signed events on our relay [openagents.trainer-card].
- Turning on **Show my level** lets other players see your level over your head in the Grid [openagents.trainer-card].
- Right now, you earn 50 XP per completed tutorial quest, and XP serves as a record, not money [openagents.earn-xp].

rows.question: how do I hide my level from other players
rows.reply: You can hide your level by going to **Account > Trainer** and choosing **Hide my level**, which replaces your published trainer profile [openagents.trainer-card]. This keeps other players in the Grid from seeing your level displayed over your head [openagents.trainer-card, openagents.verse-presence].

rows.question: What's Microcoder?
rows.reply: Microcoder is our experimental coding loop that combines Jev's typed judgments, a model, and a shared knowledge base [openagents.microcoder]. It replaced our earlier Microluna loop, and its retained Terminal-Bench passes are what the tutorial quests ask you to reproduce [openagents.microcoder]. In addition, its XP commands (`microcoder xp`) publish reproductions and link computer keys [openagents.microcoder].
